edits.new: Establish the broadest coherent explicit meaning supported by the evidence for the selected entry in a social-media post.
edits.old: Establish the explicit meaning of the selected entry in a social-media post.

edits.new:
Choose the broadest coherent meaning of the selected topic supported by its subject, context, original hierarchy and post. Breadth concerns what information belongs under this topic. Preserve its named identity, level of abstraction, expressly stated restrictions, and all explicitly named alternatives and parts. Broadening a topic does not mean replacing it with a different topic or a more general ancestor.

Use the context and hierarchy to distinguish the intended sense from details of the illustrated examples. A role, purpose, method, state or circumstance limits membership when it defines the selected topic, rather than merely describing an example of it. Do not turn a property shared by the post's examples into a requirement for the category solely because those examples share it. Ancestors help interpret the selected topic; their example-specific details do not automatically become its restrictions. Descendants illustrate narrower topics and members; they do not exhaust a broader category unless the selected subject explicitly defines that complete set. Preserve the distinction between several parts required together and alternatives admitted independently. Do not discard a named alternative or add a restriction just to fit an inferred parent meaning.

For each ambiguity between broader and narrower membership, retain an additional restriction only when the input or the defining features of the intended concept establish that it is required. When both interpretations are supported and one includes the other, choose the broader one. When interpretations concern different senses or identities rather than broader and narrower coverage of the same topic, resolve that difference from the input; do not combine them to manufacture a larger category. Evidence that identifies a particular instance retains that instance's identity; it does not make an instance into a general kind.

For an activity, state its defining action or process and any required purpose or product. Distinguish required actions from optional methods. A list of methods does not settle which actions are required. Preserve uncertainty about unmentioned methods, tools and outcomes of a particular instance; choosing a broader category does not establish facts about that instance.

The choices must form one coherent meaning. In each `resolutions.answer`, state the chosen membership condition: the properties, role, purpose or state that qualify information for the topic. Specify whether a condition characterizes the kind or must hold for the particular instance. In `justification`, explain the evidence for each retained restriction and why the chosen scope is the broadest supported interpretation. Repeating the selected subject is not enough to settle membership. If the evidence cannot establish one coherent meaning, use a null answer for the unresolved ambiguity.
edits.old:
Resolve each ambiguity using the selected subject, its context, the original branch and the post. Preserve the subject's stated boundaries and any named identity, including all explicitly named alternatives and parts of the topic. Do not discard an alternative or part solely to make the topic fit its parent. Interpret each parent-child link as an intended narrowing of the information topic, subject to the post's factual evidence. When a parent is present, choose a supported meaning of the selected topic within its parent's scope, retaining any general role, purpose or state that defines that scope. Generalize across kinds or applications satisfying those conditions; a descendant's more specific application does not remove a condition from the selected category. An ancestor's incidental details do not automatically define membership. Check whether all information covered by the selected meaning preserves the parent's required subject matter, role, purpose and state. A description requiring several parts together may narrow the topic of a required part; the other parts need not be instances of that part's kind or action. Decide whether multiple named parts must be described together or are alternatives admitted independently. Co-mention alone does not settle this. For alternatives, every admitted alternative must meet the parent's requirements. If this check fails, or preserving the relationship requires discarding part of the selected topic or adding unsupported facts, record that conflict as unresolved.

For an activity, choose a concrete condition stating its defining action or process. Decide which actions are required and which methods are optional, retaining any required purpose or product alongside the action. If competing process conditions admit different activities, record and resolve that boundary; naming the activity or listing possible methods does not settle it. For a particular instance, retain the chosen process while preserving uncertainty about unmentioned methods, tools and outcomes.

When more than one abstraction is reasonable, make a justified choice. Do not automatically choose the broadest or narrowest interpretation, or combine competing interpretations to avoid deciding. The choices must fit together as one coherent meaning. In each `resolutions.answer`, state the concrete membership condition chosen for that ambiguity: the properties, role, purpose or state that qualify something for the category. Specify whether the condition characterizes the kind or must hold for the particular example. Repeating the selected subject is not enough to resolve a difference in membership. Put the brief justification and explanations of rejected interpretations in `justification`; use a null answer if no coherent condition can be justified.
